items.title: Marty Morell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Have you read this Peter Pettinger? What he said about you? ... [INTERVIEWEE] All right I remember that, snappy.

ctx.x: But since, you know, my Bill Evans days, some recordings have come out, there are some tapes that were in the closet type of thing. And so I did get paid for those, which is kind of nice. But that’s how it was. You know like he had a story from Jimmy Cobb all the time, he recorded “Kind of Blue” you know and got $60 for the recording date. And it’s the biggest selling jazz recording in history. But that’s how things were set up. It was for the artist, the main artist. Right? And if you were a musician you got…

Have you read this Peter Pettinger? What he said about you? “Unsung stalwart of piano trio history.” That’s you. “Responsible for an exceedingly tight unit that could swing and drive relentlessly. His control of the 12-bar sections in a number like ‘Twelve Tone Tune’ for instance, snappy and precise as could be.”
All right I remember that, snappy. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
